title: Hayat and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Hayat tries to give light to Basira and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Basira, who was inner sight, insight, lived in fear of the dark, and Hayat, who carried abundant life, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Hayat's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Hayat pressed the dead lamp into Basira's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Hayat stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Hayat learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
